id_and_class.summary: Andrew Melnyk holds that phenomenal properties are real but non-fundamental: they are multiply realizable representational properties of sensations, always realized by physical properties. He argues that the hard problem is already solved because the main anti-physicalist arguments fail, and that the lingering sense that experience cannot be physical is an ‘intuition of distinctness’ produced by the way introspection works.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Qualia as Physically Realized Representational Properties

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal properties are identical to certain representational properties of sensations: the orangeness of an orange afterimage is the afterimage’s representing, in a sensory way, that something before one is orange.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Everything is either physical or physically realized. Mental properties are higher-order properties whose realizers are always physical but differ from case to case, as being poisonous is realized by cyanide in one substance and something else in antifreeze.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence (realization: given the physical realizer, the laws, and the circumstances, the mental property follows deductively, so nothing strongly emergent is added)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Melnyk grounds sensory intentionality in biological function, following Millikan’s teleosemantics. Self-consciousness is the special case in which an organism’s representations are directed at its own mental states.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia are the properties of sensations we notice when we attend to them introspectively, and Melnyk identifies them with physically realized representational properties. The burningness of a pain is the pain’s representing that part of one’s body is burning.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Fundamental physical entities and laws; higher-order properties realized by them; sensations with representational properties grounded in biological function.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Introspection presents phenomenal properties, but through conceptually encapsulated phenomenal concepts; the case for physicalism comes from empirical evidence such as the systematic dependence of experience on neural activity.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Three senses of ‘conscious’: awareness or knowledge of something, self-consciousness (introspection), and phenomenal consciousness attached to sensations, emotions, and moods.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal consciousness, introspective self-consciousness, and mental causation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Physical realization, a relation stronger than supervenience and weaker than type identity with a neural property, by which the physical realizer reductively explains the mental property.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In sensations of organisms whose physical states realize the right representational properties; since these properties are multiply realizable, they need not be tied to one neural type.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Melnyk accepts weak top-down causation: a toothache can cause you to call the dentist without overdetermination, because the mental regularity is realized by the physical one. He denies any strong top-down causation that would violate physical law.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Representation is central to the positive account: phenomenal character just is a sensory way of representing the body or the world, with content fixed by biological function.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Indirect, through teleosemantics: sensory states represent what they were selected to track.
core_claims_and_evidence: Physicalism is a broad-scope a posteriori hypothesis, supported by evidence rather than settled a priori.
Every introspectable experience has a simultaneous neural correlate, and physicalism explains this dependence more economically than dualism.

Kripke’s conceivability argument, Jackson’s knowledge argument, Levine’s explanatory gap, and Chalmers’s zombie argument are each open to serious objection, so the hard problem as precisely stated is solved.
The intuition of distinctness arises because introspection is conceptually encapsulated, so it does not track the truth and gives no reason to accept property dualism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical, supported by the empirical correlation of phenomenal and neural states and by a debunking explanation of anti-physicalist intuitions.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Melnyk concedes there is no consensus that the anti-physicalist arguments fail. Dismissing the intuition of distinctness as a cognitive illusion can look self-protective, since any contrary intuition is explained away in advance.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The intuition of distinctness persists even after it is debunked, so the theory may persuade argument without changing how experience seems. Whether token mental states are identical to physical ones is left open.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent within physicalism, treating the mental like the biological or geological as real but non-fundamental. Melnyk stresses that his representationalism is a separate proposal from his dissolution of the hard problem, and conflating the two is the most common misreading.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since phenomenal properties are multiply realizable representational properties, a non-biological system could in principle realize them, though Melnyk’s appeal to biological function leaves open what an artificial system would need.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Everything is physical or physically realized, so experience ends when its physical realizers cease.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: A thoroughgoing physicalism leaves no room for cosmic purpose in consciousness.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Multiple realizability allows that a different physical system could realize the same mental properties, though Melnyk does not address uploading.
